Deathless Frenzy.description: Starting at 4th level, a frenzied berserker can shrug off death and unconsciousness for as long as her frenzy continues. While frenzied, she does not count as disabled when at 0 hit points, nor as dying when at -1 to -9 hit points. She keeps fighting normally even if brought to -10 hit points or below, until the frenzy concludes. Once the frenzy ends, any unhealed wound effects take hold as normal. This ability offers no protection against death from massive damage or lethal spell effects such as slay living or disintegrate.

Diehard.description: At 1st level, the frenzied berserker receives Diehard as a bonus feat, regardless of whether she satisfies its normal prerequisites.

Frenzy.description: A frenzied berserker may fly into a frenzy while in combat. During this state, she receives a +6 bonus to Strength and gains one additional attack per round at her highest attack bonus when taking a full attack action. (This extra attack does not stack with haste or similar effects that provide bonus attacks.) In exchange, she suffers a -4 penalty to Armor Class and sustains 2 points of nonlethal damage each round. The frenzy persists for a number of rounds equal to 3 + her Constitution modifier. The character can try to end the frenzy early by making a DC 20 Will save as a free action once per round. A successful save immediately terminates the frenzy; a failed save means it persists. Frenzy benefits and penalties stack with those of any rage ability the character possesses. At 1st level, frenzy can be used once per day. For every two additional frenzied berserker levels gained, the character receives one more daily use of this ability (though it remains limited to one use per encounter). Entering a frenzy is a free action that can only be performed on the character's own turn, not as a reaction to someone else's action. Furthermore, whenever the character suffers damage from any source - whether an attack, spell, trap, or other effect - she automatically enters a frenzy at the beginning of her next action, provided she has at least one daily use remaining. To resist this involuntary frenzy, the character must succeed on a Will save (DC 10 + damage received since her last action) at the start of her following turn. While in a frenzy, the character is unable to use skills based on Charisma, Dexterity, or Intelligence (Intimidate being the sole exception), the Concentration skill, or any capability demanding patience or focus. She cannot cast spells, consume potions, use magic items, or read scrolls. All feats remain available to her except Combat Expertise, item creation feats, and metamagic feats. Her inspire frenzy ability functions normally. A frenzied character must direct her attacks against perceived enemies as effectively as possible. If no enemies remain before the frenzy expires, her violent rampage persists. She must then assault the nearest creature (chosen randomly if multiple creatures are equidistant), attacking without consideration for alliance, innocence, or anyone's well-being. Once the frenzy concludes, the frenzied berserker becomes fatigued (-2 penalty to Strength and Dexterity, unable to charge or run) for the remainder of the encounter. If a rage ability is still active when the frenzy ends, the fatigue is postponed until the rage also concludes - at which point the character becomes exhausted rather than merely fatigued.

Greater Frenzy.description: Upon reaching 8th level, the Strength bonus granted by frenzy increases to +10, replacing the normal +6 bonus.

Improved Power Attack.description: From 5th level on, when the frenzied berserker uses the Power Attack feat, she deals +3 to melee damage for every -2 penalty applied to her melee attack rolls (or +3 per -1 penalty when wielding a two-handed weapon that is not a double weapon). This replaces rather than stacks with the standard Power Attack damage trade.

Inspire Frenzy.description: At 6th level, while in a frenzy herself, a frenzied berserker can spread that frenzy to nearby allies. All willing allies within 10 feet receive the full benefits and drawbacks of frenzy as though they possessed the ability. The inspired frenzy in affected allies lasts for a number of rounds equal to 3 + the frenzied berserker's Constitution modifier, irrespective of whether they stay within the 10-foot radius. The character gains an additional daily use of this ability for every two frenzied berserker levels beyond 6th, but it can still only be activated once per encounter.

Supreme Cleave.description: From 2nd level onward, a frenzied berserker may take a 5-foot step between individual attacks while using Cleave or Great Cleave. This movement is still restricted to one 5-foot adjustment per round, so it cannot be used in a round where she has already taken a 5-foot step.

Supreme Power Attack.description: At 10th level, when employing Power Attack, the frenzied berserker gains +2 to melee damage for every -1 penalty she accepts on melee attack rolls (or +4 per -1 penalty when using a two-handed weapon other than a double weapon). This benefit replaces and does not stack with Power Attack or Improved Power Attack.

Tireless Frenzy.description: At 10th level, the frenzied berserker is no longer subject to fatigue when a frenzy ends. She continues to suffer the 2 points of nonlethal damage per round for the frenzy's duration as normal.

Weapon and Armor Proficiency.description: This prestige class does not grant proficiency with any weapons or armor.

classFeatures.description: A frenzied berserker can enter a frenzy during combat. While frenzied, she gains a +6 bonus to Strength and, if she makes a full attack action, gains a single extra attack each round at her highest bonus. (This latter effect is not cumulative with haste or other effects that grant additional attacks.) However, she also takes a -4 penalty to Armor Class and takes 2 points of nonlethal damage per round. A frenzy lasts for a number of rounds equal to 3 + the frenzied berserker's Constitution modifier. To end the frenzy before its duration expires, the character may attempt a DC 20 Will save once per round as a free action. Success ends the frenzy immediately; failure means it continues. The effects of frenzy stack with those from any rage ability the character may have. At 1st level, the character can enter a frenzy once per day. Thereafter, she gains one additional use per day of this ability for every two frenzied berserker levels she acquires (but she can't use the ability more than once in any encounter). The character can enter a frenzy as a free action. Even though this takes no time, she can do it only during her turn, not in response to another's action. In addition, if she takes damage from an attack, spell, trap, or any other source, she automatically enters a frenzy at the start of her next action, as long as she still has at least one daily usage of the ability left. To avoid entering a frenzy in response to a provoking effect, the character must make a successful Will save (DC 10 + points of damage taken since her last action) at the start of her next turn. While frenzied, the character cannot use any Charisma-, Dexterity-, or Intelligence-based skills (except for Intimidate), the Concentration skill, or any abilities that require patience or concentration, nor can she cast spells, drink potions, activate magic items, or read scrolls. She can use any feat she has except Combat Expertise, item creation feats, or metamagic feats. She can use her special ability to inspire frenzy normally. During a frenzy, the frenzied berserker must attack those she perceives as foes to the best of her ability. Should she run out of enemies before her frenzy expires, her rampage continues. She must then attack the nearest creature (determine randomly if several potential foes are equidistant) and fight that opponent without regard to friendship, innocence, or health (the target's or her own). When a frenzy ends, the frenzied berserker is fatigued (-2 penalty to Strength and Dexterity, unable to charge or run) for the duration of the encounter. If the character is still under the effect of a rage ability, the fatigued condition does not apply until the rage ends-at which point the character is exhausted, not merely fatigued.
